is_public.rule: ipaddress is_global after unwrapping ::ffff:a.b.c.d, and not multicast, reserved or site-local
is_public._note: ipaddress reports is_global True for the multicast vectors 224.0.0.1 and ff02::1 and for the unallocated 4000::1 and the site-local fec0::1 (Python 3.14.6); none is public. For every other address public == ipaddress is_global of the unwrapped address, so a property test compares with this rule (is_global and not multicast, reserved or site-local), not with is_global alone (O7-R48 M1).

hosts._note: Public addresses are 93.184.216.x, which ipaddress reports is_global (the documentation ranges 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.0/24 are not global, so they are not used for public hosts); build.py asserts is_global for every address labelled public and not-global (after unwrapping ::ffff:a.b.c.d) for every address labelled private (O7-R46). Nothing dials these addresses. A host is public only when every address it resolves to is public. Host probes use https://<host>/probe fetched with manifest_hosts = #manifest_hosts plus the probe host.

records._note: locator rule (O7-R48 H2): a url row's locator must pass the fence header rule (prompts/fence.py:36, [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:+/-]*), so it cannot hold ?, =, & or %; the row's locator, not its url, goes in the header. Row 2 carries a distinct locator for that reason; every other url row's locator is its url. Attempted fetches only: a row refused by its own date is never fetched and has no record (O7-R48 L3).

sentences: An item dated after the cutoff is refused. The cutoff is the earlier of the as-of date and the context's `run.cutoff`; with no `run.cutoff` it is the as-of date.

A URL row is fetched only when the run names a user ruling that lifts the live-provider pause for `web-retrieval` (`research_ruling`); without one every URL row is refused before anything is written, and the refusal names the ruling the run needs. A fetched item is `https` only, from the user's manifest, with every address public, at most three redirects, the same byte cap, and a recorded url, address, status, size and hash in `research/fetches.json`; a publication date found in the response can refuse an item, never admit one.
No provider or credential is used; the web is used only to fetch the user's URL rows under the ruling Intake names, and the readiness ceiling is `RESEARCH_READY`.
Each research item names a file or an `https` url, a family, a publication date, a locator and the tag `research`.
